_comment: Curated, publicly traded 13F institutional filers. Every CIK is resolved live through SecEdgarClient.ticker_map() from the ticker below at run time - never a hand-typed CIK - so a wrong or delisted ticker degrades to 'no data for this manager' rather than silently reading a different filer's holdings under this name. Necessarily partial: large, influential 13F filers that are privately held (Renaissance Technologies, Citadel Advisors, Bridgewater, ...) have no ticker and are not reachable this way. Expand by adding tickers, not CIKs.
_style_comment: 'style' matters because it is not a random subset of institutional flow. The largest managers here (BlackRock, State Street, Invesco) run AUM dominated by index funds and ETFs - their quarter-over-quarter position changes are close to mechanically determined by index membership and fund flows, not conviction, and feeding that into a research score that already carries valuation and sector-percentile inputs would partly reintroduce market-cap/size as a hidden second input under a 'smart money' label. build_institutional_screen.py defaults to style=active only for exactly this reason. 'alternative' (private-equity/alternative-asset managers) is excluded from the default sleeve too: their public-equity 13F stakes are typically residual holdings from take-privates or specific strategic positions, lumpy and idiosyncratic rather than a portfolio-flow signal comparable to a mutual-fund manager's.
